observation.visible_scene: A black-crowned night heron stands in shallow, clear water over a bed of rounded pebbles, with a dark mirror-image reflection directly beneath it and a cluster of floating green aquatic plants at the left edge. The bird balances on one planted leg while the other foot is held raised above the surface with its long toes splayed; this one-legged, raised-foot stance is maintained across the entire excerpt. The bird's black cap, red eye, gray folded wing, and white underparts remain clearly visible throughout.
visible_changes: The head-and-neck posture changes progressively: for roughly the first half of the clip (frames 1–22) the neck is held upright and vertical, then from about t≈1.4–1.5 s onward the neck bends forward and the head lowers into a more horizontal, hunched alignment, making the pale stripe on the back more prominent.
The reflection below the bird deforms in step with this neck/head tilt, its mirrored head moving forward as the real head lowers.
The raised, splayed foot stays lifted above the water for the whole segment; no footfall or weight transfer to that foot occurs within the clip.

There is a small apparent shift of the bird and the underwater pebbles toward the left of the frame by the end, suggesting a slight camera pan/zoom, though the bird's feet remain over essentially the same water location.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the forward neck lean develops into a strike, a step, or flight after the clip ends.
Whether the raised-foot pose was already mid-motion at the start or had just been adopted.
What caused the bird to lower its head during the segment.
uncertain_details: Whether the slight change in framing is camera motion or a small shift of the bird's standing position—background pebble evidence is limited.
The precise frame at which the neck tilt begins (around t≈1.4–1.5 s).
The exact angle/position of the lifted foot relative to the water surface is hard to judge because it partly overlaps the reflection.
